business_summary: Eli Lilly discovers, manufactures and sells prescription medicines. Patients (mostly in the US) get them by prescription; the money actually comes from insurers, employers, pharmacy-benefit managers and government programs, and increasingly straight from patients through Lilly's own LillyDirect self-pay channel. The company is now overwhelmingly an incretin (GLP-1 / GIP) business: tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for type-2 diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, produced $9,943M + $4,928M = $14,871M of the $22,974M of Q2 2026 revenue, i.e. about 65% of the company (10-Q, three months ended 2026-06-30). In April 2026 the FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron), the first small-molecule oral GLP-1 pill for weight management, which did $98M in its first partial quarter. Outside obesity/diabetes Lilly sells oncology (Verzenio $1,474M in Q2 2026, Jaypirca, Inluriyo), immunology (Taltz $856M, Ebglyss, Omvoh), cardiometabolic (Jardiance $1,232M, Trulicity $1,219M) and neuroscience (Kisunla for Alzheimer's). Full-year 2025 revenue was $65,179M and management now guides 2026 revenue to $85-87B. Why it should still be winning in 5-10 years: obesity and its comorbidities are a very large, under-treated, chronic (i.e. repeat-purchase) market; tirzepatide's composition-of-matter patent runs to roughly January 2036; Lilly has spent years and tens of billions building peptide fill-finish capacity that competitors cannot rent; and the pipeline behind tirzepatide (orforglipron oral GLP-1, retatrutide triple agonist with a BLA planned for Q1 2027, bimagrumab for muscle preservation) is the deepest in the category.

moat.type: Intangible assets: patents and regulatory exclusivity on tirzepatide (composition-of-matter to ~Jan 2036) and orforglipron; a decade-long, multi-billion-dollar clinical-evidence lead (Zepbound beat Novo's CagriSema head-to-head, 24% vs 20% weight loss over 84 weeks); very hard-to-replicate peptide and oral-solid manufacturing scale (capex $9.9B TTM vs $2.1B of D&A, plus a further $4.5B Indiana commitment announced with Q2 2026); brand and prescriber habit in obesity; growing direct-to-patient distribution (LillyDirect / TrumpRx) that Lilly controls end to end.

quality.gross_margin: 83.0% FY2025 (revenue $65,179M less cost of sales $11,052M); 85.8% in Q2 2026 (revenue $22,974M less cost of sales $3,268M); 83.4% on TTM to 2026-06-30
quality.roic: ~34% (TTM to 2026-06-30 NOPAT ~$26.7B = pretax income $33,595M x (1 - 20.5% effective tax) divided by ending invested capital ~$79.8B = total debt $54,908M + equity $33,879M - cash $8,950M); ~38% on average invested capital. Analyst-computed from filed XBRL line items, not a company-reported figure.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: ~1.3x (net debt $45,958M at 2026-06-30 = debt $54,908M less cash $8,950M; divided by TTM EBITDA proxy ~$35.7B = pretax income $33,595M + D&A $2,099M; interest expense is NOT added back, so the true ratio is slightly lower). Analyst-computed from filed XBRL line items.
quality.fcf_positive: yes - TTM to 2026-06-30 operating cash flow $28,083M less capex $9,893M = FCF ~$18,190M (~$20.33/diluted share on 894.8M shares). FY2025 was $16,813M - $7,841M = $8,972M. FCF is materially depressed relative to earnings by the manufacturing build-out.

valuation.method: pe + fcf_yield, averaged by code/valuation.py. PE: FY2026 company EPS guidance midpoint $36.00 (guided range $35.50-$36.50, reported and non-GAAP, after a $3.03 acquired-IPR&D charge) x multiples 24 / 29 / 34 -> $864 / $1,044 / $1,224. FCF yield: TTM FCF/diluted share $20.33 at target yields 3.5% / 2.8% / 2.2% -> $581 / $726 / $924. Multiples chosen because a wide-moat pharma compounding earnings >30% with roughly a decade of composition-of-matter protection deserves a clear premium to the market (~34x at the high end), while the eventual tirzepatide patent cliff and US/ex-US price erosion argue against paying a perpetual growth multiple (24x at the low end). The FCF-yield leg is deliberately conservative and acts as a floor: current free cash flow is held down by growth capex ($9.9B TTM against $2.1B of depreciation), so it understates normalized cash generation.

bull_case: Category leadership in the largest new drug market in a generation: Mounjaro grew 91% to $9,943M and Zepbound 46% to $4,928M in Q2 2026, together ~65% of company revenue, and total revenue grew 48% year over year to $22,974M.

Best-in-class efficacy is now proven head-to-head: Novo Nordisk's CagriSema delivered ~20% weight loss over 84 weeks versus ~24% for Lilly's Zepbound in a direct Phase 3 comparison (Feb 2026), and CagriSema also lost to tirzepatide on blood-sugar control.
Extraordinary unit economics: 85.8% gross margin in Q2 2026, ~34% ROIC on TTM figures, guided 2026 performance margin of 49.0-50.5% (raised from 47.0-48.5%).

Format expansion, not just volume: Foundayo (orforglipron) was FDA-approved 2026-04-01 as the first oral GLP-1 for weight management with no food or water restrictions and booked $98M in a partial first quarter - a pill scales to primary care and to markets injectables cannot reach.

A real pipeline behind the franchise: retatrutide's clinical package is complete with a BLA planned for Q1 2027 across obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain; olomorasib received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in KRAS G12C pancreatic cancer.
Long IP runway: tirzepatide composition-of-matter protection runs to about January 2036, with formulation and device patents claimed beyond that.

Balance sheet can fund the build: net debt ~$46.0B against a TTM EBITDA proxy of ~$35.7B (~1.3x) while still paying a dividend ($3.46/share declared in H1 2026) and buying back stock ($4,108M in FY2025).
risks: Valuation is the headline risk. At $1,185.96 the stock is ~34% ABOVE our base fair value of $885 and above the high end of our band ($1,074). At the guided FY2026 EPS midpoint of $36.00 that is ~33x forward earnings. We are being asked to pay for many years of flawless execution.

Extreme single-molecule concentration: tirzepatide (Mounjaro + Zepbound) was 56% of FY2025 revenue and ~65% of Q2 2026 revenue. Any safety signal, manufacturing failure or legal setback on one molecule would hit the majority of the company.

Price is falling fast even as volume explodes. Q2 2026 revenue growth of 48% came from a 60% volume increase partly offset by a 13% decline in realized prices; US prices fell ~9% and international realized prices fell 36%, largely from Mounjaro's addition to China's NRDL.

Government pricing policy is now directly in the P&L. Under the November 2025 agreement with the US administration, injectable tirzepatide is priced at $245/month for Medicare (with $50 patient copays) and roughly $346/month average via TrumpRx, versus a former list price above $1,080. Further most-favored-nation extension, or eventual IRA Medicare negotiation of tirzepatide, would compress this further.

Generic challengers have arrived earlier than the 2036 patent date implies: Sandoz had two tirzepatide ANDAs accepted by the FDA (announced 2026-06-29) and China's Hybio announced accepted ANDAs plus a Paragraph IV challenge to Lilly's tirzepatide patents (July 2026). Lilly should win, but litigation outcomes are never certain and headlines will be volatile.

Free cash flow conversion is weak relative to earnings: TTM FCF of ~$18.2B against ~$26.7B of TTM net income, because capex is running at ~$9.9B TTM with another $4.5B of Indiana/genetic-medicine capacity just committed. If obesity demand slows, that capacity becomes stranded fixed cost.
Business-development spending is lumpy and dilutive to reported earnings: acquired in-process R&D charges cut $3.03 off FY2026 EPS guidance, and $3,486M of IPR&D purchases were made in H1 2026 alone.

Litigation and product-liability tail: the 10-Q discloses consolidated Mounjaro/Zepbound product-liability proceedings in Pennsylvania federal court, a Verzenio ANDA challenge from Cipla, the Emgality/Teva patent dispute, 340B litigation and the insulin-pricing MDL.

Competition does not stand still: Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Roche/Zealand, AstraZeneca and Chinese biotechs all have incretin programs; an oral or monthly competitor with comparable efficacy and a lower price would compress the whole category's economics.
what_would_break_thesis: Combined Mounjaro + Zepbound revenue declines year over year for two consecutive quarters (the franchise has stopped growing).
Company gross margin falls below 75% for two consecutive quarters (from 85.8% in Q2 2026) - i.e. price concessions are outrunning volume.
Total revenue declines year over year for two consecutive quarters, or full-year revenue shrinks in any year.
Net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 2.5x (from ~1.3x at 2026-06-30) - the manufacturing build-out is being financed beyond what cash flow supports.
Free cash flow is negative for a full fiscal year, or TTM FCF falls below 40% of TTM net income for four consecutive quarters (from ~68% today).
ROIC falls below 15% on a trailing-twelve-month basis (from ~34%).
A court invalidates or holds not-infringed a core tirzepatide composition-of-matter patent, or Lilly settles to allow US generic tirzepatide entry before 2033.
An FDA safety action on tirzepatide or orforglipron - a boxed warning, a label restriction that materially narrows the eligible population, or a withdrawal.
A retatrutide or orforglipron pivotal-program failure or FDA rejection that removes the next leg of growth.

US net realized price for the incretin franchise falls more than 25% year over year in any single year (beyond the ~9% US decline reported in Q2 2026), from MFN extension, IRA negotiation, or competitive discounting.
Management withdraws or cuts full-year revenue guidance by more than 10% versus the prior guide.
A serious accounting restatement, auditor change under dispute, or other material governance red flag.
catalysts: Retatrutide BLA submission planned for Q1 2027 across obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain.
Orforglipron (Foundayo) ramp through LillyDirect, retail pharmacy and telehealth, plus a potential type-2 diabetes label.
Broader Medicare/Medicaid obesity coverage arriving under the November 2025 pricing agreement - volume in exchange for price.
New capacity coming online (the additional $4.5B Indiana and genetic-medicine investment) relieving the supply constraint.
Resolution of the Sandoz / Hybio tirzepatide ANDA challenges in Lilly's favour.
A price pullback toward the $1,074 high end - or better, the $885 base - of our fair-value band, which would open a real margin of safety.
